title: First after Op Sindoor: India invites Pak to SCO meeting in Delhi
syllabus: GS2 › India and its neighbourhood – relations; Important international institutions, agencies and fora (SCO)
summary: India has invited Pakistan's culture minister to the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi (20–21 November), the first invite to a senior Pakistani minister since Operation Sindoor.
ideas: Bilateral freeze, multilateral engagement: no direct talks with Pakistan, but contact at the SCO, where the host must invite all members.

The SCO is where India raises common issues with Pakistan and Central Asia; Pakistan hosts the next summit.
The SCO gives India a forum to push 'connectivity, transit and trade' that bilateral channels with Pakistan cannot.

practice.q: Despite frozen bilateral ties, India continues to engage Pakistan through the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). Discuss the significance of such multilateral engagement for India.
parts: Introduction: frozen ties, yet SCO engagement (one line, with facts)
India's engagement with Pakistan at the SCO (multi-dimensional)
Significance of multilateral engagement for India

answer.t: Despite ties frozen since Pathankot–Uri (2016) and Op Sindoor (2025), India has invited Pakistan's culture minister to the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, New Delhi (Nov 2026).

answer.h: How India engages Pakistan through the SCO

pts.t: An SCO host must invite all members, so engagement follows the rules of the grouping rather than signalling a thaw.
Ministers meet at SCO events even when bilateral visits are off.
pts.ex: Bilawal Bhutto in Goa, 2023; Jaishankar in Islamabad, 2024.

pts.t: Both sit in the SCO's counter-terror framework, where India can press its concerns on terror.
Pakistan lies on India's shortest land route to Afghanistan and Central Asia.
pts.ex: India flagged 'connectivity, transit and trade' in Islamabad, 2026.

pts.t: The SCO keeps regional trade on the agenda while bilateral trade is suspended.
A low-risk track built on shared heritage, not disputed politics.
pts.ex: Civilisational Dialogue proposed by PM Modi at Tianjin, 2025.

answer.h: Significance of multilateral engagement for India

pts.t: India stays firm on terror without looking isolationist or blocking regional cooperation.
The SCO balances India's partnerships with the West (Quad) with a seat among Russia, China and Central Asia.
Multilateral forums let India put cross-border terror before Pakistan's partners.
Central Asia offers energy and markets; the SCO complements routes such as INSTC and Chabahar.
Proposing and hosting initiatives lets India set the agenda instead of reacting.
Civilisational diplomacy projects India's cultural depth and builds goodwill beyond governments.
No forum can sustain engagement through repeated attacks.
China's weight and closeness to Pakistan can tilt SCO positions against India.
pts.ex: CPEC through PoK, which India opposes.

pts.k: Bilateral disputes brought into a multilateral forum
pts.t: Pakistan uses SCO platforms to push its Kashmir narrative, against the SCO's norm of keeping bilateral issues out.
pts.ex: India's NSA walked out of an SCO NSA meeting (2020) over Pakistan's distorted map.

pts.t: Pakistan blocks India's land route to Afghanistan and Central Asia, limiting the SCO's connectivity promise.
Every member has a veto, so terror language gets diluted.
pts.ex: India declined the SCO Defence Ministers' statement (June 2025) as it omitted Pahalgam.

pts.k: Divergence on the Belt and Road
pts.t: India stays out of SCO endorsements of BRI on sovereignty grounds, isolating it on connectivity texts.
Use RATS and SCO declarations to name cross-border terror; no dilution for consensus.
Keep cultural and multilateral channels open, but tie any bilateral step to verifiable action on terror.
Push Chabahar, INSTC and the Ashgabat route to reach Central Asia without Pakistan.
Work with Russia and Central Asian members on terror, Afghanistan and connectivity.
Build on the India–Central Asia Summit and Dialogue formats.
Use India's SECURE SCO vision (security, economy, connectivity, unity, sovereignty, environment) to frame initiatives.

answer.t: 'Bilateral freeze, multilateral engagement' keeps the door ajar for India without lowering its guard on terror.

trend.t: UPSC has moved from India–Pakistan as a bilateral issue (2015, 2016) to the groupings and regions around it: the SCO (2021, 2023) and Central Asia (2018, 2024). The newer questions ask about India's role, not just facts about the grouping.
trend.watch: The SCO has come twice in three years (2021, 2023) and Central Asia twice (2018, 2024). When you study international organisations, the SCO and India's Central Asia policy are must-study topics.
